Head 0 of layer 0’s keys, columns 0, 1, 2 and 127. Row p0 is the same four numbers at every step — a past token’s K never changes, so v2 keeps it and v1.5 rebuilds it.

text.tspan: D · What it saves, and what it costs
position passes through the decoder to write n tokens
position through both layers, every sub-layer
what the cache holds for one sentence
The work saved is pushing past positions back through every projection and feed-forward block. What stays is attention itself: the new query still meets every cached key, so
over a whole answer attention grows with n², just with a much smaller constant. The price is memory that grows with every token — and with every beam.
